newsitem.title: FRANCE: France probing irregularities at Credit Foncier.
newsitem.headline: France probing irregularities at Credit Foncier.

text.p: The Paris public prosecutor is investigating alleged financial irregularities at loss-making property loans company Credit Foncier in 1992-94, Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure told parliament on Wednesday.

"An investigation is under way...on counts of distributing fictitious dividends, presenting inaccurate accounts and illegal conflict of interest covering 1992, 1993 and 1994 at Credit Foncier. Justice will be done," he told the National Assembly.
Credit Foncier reported a 1995 loss of 10.8 billion francs earlier this year and Finance Minister Jean Arthuis announced a plan in July to "nationalise" the company and wind it down.
He said at the time there had been "reckless errors" in the past and the new management had requested a legal investigation.

State-owned bank Caisse des Depots et des Consignations has since taken over the group at the government's behest to prepare for a wind-down but the plan has run into stiff resistance from unions and politicians who blame past management for its woes.

While the group was private and listed on the stock market, the government was in charge of appointing top managers because of Credit Foncier's role in providing low-cost housing loans on behalf of the state.
